title: Inner Child Sense Read
intro: Before your guide goes into the post, fresh readers read every word of it for sense, one part each, looking for a real word where another belongs, like "oily" for "old" in your hypnosis guide. To test them, I hid nine errors of that kind in their copies, and they found eight. The ninth, "wealth" where "warmth" belonged, was in the last part, and a second reader of that part missed it too, so there their silence counts for a little less. Everything they found is in your own words, so nothing changes without you: 10 cards are typos or slips, 6 may not be the word you meant, 2 make your spelling and dashes match, 1 is a question, and 2 are ones I'd leave.
A spell check under the read found nothing else to fix: every word it didn't know is a name, a term, or one of your own words.
Approve, Reject or Revise each card, with a comment if you like. Your answers save as you click. When you're done, tell me in the chat, and I'll put them in.

slip.label: Typo or slip
slip.about: A word, a letter or a mark that is clearly off: a typo, a missing word, a quote mark in the wrong place.

meaning.label: Maybe not the word you meant
meaning.about: A real word where, read closely, another seems meant. Only you know which word you meant, so Revise if mine is not it.

form.label: Spelling and dashes
form.about: Your own spelling and dash, made the same everywhere.

leave.label: A reader flagged it; I would leave it
leave.about: A reader found these; I would leave them as they are. Open one to overrule me.

suggestions.title: Unfortunate, or Unfortunately

edits.before: Céline's song is called On ne change pas – "we don't change." I think that's both fortunately, and unfortunately, true for most of us. Fortunately in the sense that the sweet, innocent, curious, vivacious little one is still inside us, even if hiding. Unfortunate in the sense that we often don't truly develop the adult qualities that we might pretend to have, so we continue burdening that little one inside us with troubles they aren't made for handling. This shows up in how we may feel abandoned, helpless, impulsive, frightened, or desperate to be chosen.

suggestions.title: Two double hyphens

edits.before: And I realized that it doesn't make sense to ask the child to "heal itself," which is really a disguised request for the child to abandon its own nature and turn into an adult. I call that "forced adulthood," where the child has to deal with situations the evolved inner adult should be handling--we see this in actual children all the time when their parents are not providing care. People even wear t-shirts saying, "I don't wanna adult today." The forced adulting often goes along with a misperception that there is something wrong with the inner child. Instead, we need to separately develop the qualities of a good inner parent for that rightly vulnerable child: the loving Nurturer, safe Protector, and wise Guide.

On the other hand, I've noticed that I can sometimes completely flip a bad psychedelic trip into a good one with gratitude alone.

suggestions.title: Feel like yours, then become your own

Continuing to relate to benevolent spiritual powers/beings is still perfectly fine, but they would surely be happy if they rubbed off on you! suggestions.title: Bring someone mighty down

edits.before: Be honest with yourself about what your goal is for this communication. Do you want to break someone mighty down? To show that you or your views matter? suggestions.title: Call yourself out first

edits.before: But Jesus also said to take the log out of your own eye first, and then "you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye." That's exactly what made Tyler the right person to say something. If you actually have the problem they have, and you want to call them out for it, call yourself out for it instead. I'd ask you to please have some compassion for him. I have a young child now, so this really touches me." Tyler's an evangelical Christian who preaches on YouTube, so the fact that he really appreciated this take on Jesus' message is pretty salient to me.
